reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 13 --verse 5.87. After the three reported views of al-iʿtidaʾ (al-Suddi: Uthman b. Mazʿun's intended self-castration; Ikrima: the companions' forbidding of women, food, dress, sleep; al-Hasan: passing from lawful to forbidden), Abu Jaʿfar's own paragraph (qala Abu Jaʿfar) makes 'la taʿtadu' general, no one may overstep God's bound in what He made lawful or forbidden; the next paragraph says those who resolved to forbid themselves the lawful were reproached only (innama) for passing beyond what was laid down. All three evidence pieces string-match. The sentence's 'reproached for just that' refers back to overstepping, which is exactly his innama clause; he calls the Uthman occasion only 'not impossible', and the sentence does not assert the occasion, only the reproach, which he does assert. His heading opens 5:87 separately inside a seg labelled 5:86 to 5:87, so 'on 5:87' is his place. Plain sense checked in day.js: 5:87 addresses the believers, 5:88 food, 5:89 oaths, 5:90 to 5:91 strong drink; no four-word run from the key. No school, no comparison (his Christians/monks report is left out), no hard passage. verse.js ok (Al-Ma'idah 5:87, at 755, 24 words); entry-check.js ok, no errors or warns.
